Exercise A

Read & Spot

Read the text and choose the correct reported form for each gap.

Before you read

This question is not marked - just write what comes to mind.

The Class Survey

How it works: when you report speech, the verb usually goes one step back — "I love music" → Ben said he loved music. "I have finished" → she said she had finished.

1 Ben that he loved music more than sport.

2 Aylin said she her project the night before.

3 The twins said they a film when the teacher called.

4 Jonas said he cake for the next school party.

5 Maria said she such a boring film before.

6 And Leon said he like surveys at all.

Exercise B

Report the Statements

Each quote goes one step back in time. Choose the correct reported form.

Task

1 "I am tired," she said. → She said she tired.

2 "We will win," they said. → They said they win.

3 "I have lost my keys," he said. → He said he his keys.

4 "We are playing tonight," they said. → They said they that night.

5 "I can drive," she said. → She said she drive.

6 "We went home early," they said. → They said they home early.

7 "I must leave now," he said. → He said he leave.

8 "We may stay," they said. → They said they stay.

Exercise C

Questions & Commands

Reported questions use statement word order — and commands become told/asked + infinitive.

Task

1 "Where do you live?" → She asked me where I .

2 "Do you like coffee?" → He asked me I liked coffee.

3 "Don't talk during the test!" → The teacher told us talk during the test.

4 "Please help me." → She asked me help her.

5 "Don't touch the wet paint!" → He told me touch it.

6 "When does the train leave?" → She asked when the train .

Exercise D

Writing

Report a real conversation.

Task

Think of four things people said to you this week (or invent them). Write a short report (6-8 sentences) for a class blog called "Overheard This Week": report at least three statements and one question. Start like this: On Monday, my brother told me ...
